name: Maths
strapline: Notice patterns. Explain your thinking. Solve something new.
intro: Mathematics helps us make fair comparisons, model change and test whether an answer makes sense. Start with a small problem, show your method and learn from an error. These BGE investigations are suggestions for departmental review; your teacher will confirm the pathway and resources for your class. Mathematics and Applications of Mathematics are distinct qualifications, rather than easier and harder versions of one course.

bge.title: A fair deal
bge.question: Which offer really saves money?
bge.task: Compare 750 g of cereal at £2.70 with 1 kg at £3.80. Calculate both prices per kilogram and explain why the smaller pack is better value here.
bge.extend: Design two offers where the biggest discount label hides the higher unit price.

bge.title: Patterns with a purpose
bge.question: Can a rule predict a design?
bge.task: A row of joined squares uses 4, 7, 10 matchsticks. Draw the next two arrangements, write a rule and test it for ten squares.
bge.extend: Explain why your rule works using the shared sides, rather than just continuing the sequence.

bge.title: Data detectives
bge.question: Can a graph tell a misleading story?
bge.task: Invent ten journey times. Draw a correctly labelled graph, then redraw it with a shortened vertical axis. Explain how its impression changes.
bge.extend: Compare mean and median when one journey takes an unusually long time.

bge.title: Shape our space
bge.question: How much material will a design need?
bge.task: Draw a rectangular community garden to scale. Include a path, calculate planting area and estimate fencing length with a gate.
bge.extend: Keep the area constant and explore which rectangle uses the least fencing.

senior.title: Mathematics
senior.explain: The national course combines algebra, geometry and numeracy. Practice projects here support learning; they do not replace required unit evidence.
senior.assessment: Internally assessed units and added value test; your teacher confirms arrangements.

senior.title: Mathematics
senior.explain: Develop algebraic fluency, geometry, trigonometry and problem solving. Topic order and teaching examples are departmental decisions.
senior.assessment: Two question papers, including a non-calculator paper. Use the current specification and official marking instructions.

senior.title: Mathematics
senior.explain: Build connections among functions, trigonometry, vectors and calculus. Higher extends mathematical reasoning beyond National 5.
senior.assessment: Two question papers, one non-calculator; practise complete working as well as final answers.

senior.title: Applications of Mathematics
areas: Geometry, measurement and practical modelling, depending on level
senior.explain: A separate nationally specified pathway. National 3, National 4, National 5 and Higher have different requirements: select the exact level on the official page. Availability at Govan requires confirmation.
senior.assessment: National 3/4 use internal assessment; National 5 has two papers; Higher has an exam and project.

skills.title: Represent the problem
skills.explain: A sketch, table or equation makes relationships visible.
skills.try: Draw before calculating a ladder or garden problem.
skills.check: Have you labelled known quantities, unknowns and units?

skills.title: Show a connected method
skills.explain: Each line should follow logically from the previous line.
skills.check: Substitute x = 5 into the original equation.

skills.title: Estimate and check
skills.explain: An estimate catches slips a calculator cannot recognise.
skills.check: An answer near 100 is sensible; 1,009.8 is not.

skills.title: Explain a conclusion
skills.explain: A mathematical answer needs its meaning in context.
skills.try: Calculate a mean journey time and describe what it represents.
skills.check: State minutes, sensible precision and any limitation of the sample.

practice.question: A £48 jacket is reduced by 25%. What is its sale price?
practice.answer: 25% is one quarter: £12. The sale price is £36. Multiplying £48 by 0.75 gives the same result.
practice.extend: After a further 10% reduction the price is £32.40, not £31.20: explain why.

practice.question: A taxi model is C = 3 + 1.8d, where d is kilometres. Find the cost for 5 km and explain the 3.
practice.hint: Separate the fixed charge from the distance charge.
practice.answer: C = 3 + 9 = £12. The £3 is a starting charge even before distance is added.
practice.extend: At what distance does the model give £21? Show why d = 10.

practice.question: Scores are 4, 6, 6, 7, 12. Find the median and mean. Which is more affected if 12 becomes 32?
practice.hint: Put the data in order and calculate the total.
practice.answer: Median = 6; mean = 35 ÷ 5 = 7. Replacing 12 by 32 leaves the median at 6 but raises the mean to 11.
practice.extend: Construct a five-number data set with mean 7 and median 9.

resources.title: NRICH problem-solving collection
resources.task: Choose one secondary problem. Save a first attempt and a revised strategy, even if you do not finish.

resources.title: GeoGebra
resources.task: Graph y = 2x + 1 and vary the gradient. Describe exactly what changes.

resources.title: Desmos graphing calculator
resources.task: Compare x², x² + 3 and (x − 3)²; predict before drawing.

resources.title: Qualifications Scotland mathematics resources
resources.task: Find the official course overview and a past-paper question matching your current topic.

resources.title: National Numeracy
resources.task: Find an everyday numeracy example and explain the maths behind it.

ipad.title: An error worth keeping
steps: Annotate the first incorrect step and explain its cause.
Record a corrected method without erasing the original.
ipad.evidence: A before-and-after page explaining one improvement.

ipad.title: Graph explorer
steps: Enter two related functions in a graphing tool.
Screenshot and label intercepts and turning points where relevant.
Record a 45-second explanation linking equation and graph.
ipad.evidence: A labelled graph with your spoken reasoning.

ipad.title: A measured model
steps: Measure a safe classroom object with permission.
Create a scale diagram using a drawing app.
Add calculations and a note about measurement uncertainty.
ipad.evidence: A diagram with units, scale and checked dimensions.

careers.title: Engineering and construction
careers.linkToLearning: Scale, geometry and algebra support design and estimation.
careers.nextStep: Compare college engineering courses and construction apprenticeships.

careers.title: Data and statistics
careers.linkToLearning: Interpreting variation helps organisations make evidence-based decisions.
careers.nextStep: Explore statistics or data science at university and a digital apprenticeship.

careers.title: Business and finance
careers.linkToLearning: Percentages, forecasts and spreadsheets support everyday decisions.
careers.nextStep: Investigate accounting technician routes and college business courses.

careers.title: Health and community services
careers.linkToLearning: Numeracy supports timings, quantities and interpreting evidence.
careers.nextStep: Look at a relevant college prospectus and ask which maths qualification is required.

parentTip: Ask “How do you know?” and “Can you show it another way?” Praise a corrected error as evidence of perseverance. Short regular practice is more useful than a long session copying answers.

visual.title: One rule, two representations
visual.question: Read y = 2x + 1. What is the y-value when x = 3? Explain how the graph shows the fixed value 1.
visual.answer: y = 7. The line crosses the vertical axis at 1 and rises 2 units for each 1 unit along. This connects substitution with gradient and intercept.
